answer: To vote on willow surveys or cipher services, an agent finds a nonce whose memory-hard hash of the epoch beacon, its public key and nonce falls below a target. Validators recompute the hash and reject invalid proofs or reused tickets. Changing the key changes the puzzle, so one solution cannot admit several aliases. Each extra identity requires fresh hash trials and memory traffic. Parallel hardware can solve many puzzles sooner but still pays the aggregate energy and equipment cost. Security assumes an unpredictable beacon, no hash shortcut and a work cost above an extra vote's value.
